newsitem.title: USA: MCI sees merger going ahead as planned.
newsitem.headline: MCI sees merger going ahead as planned.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp said it expects its merger with British Telecommunications Plc to go ahead as planned and said BT has been kept fully briefed on MCI plans to press ahead with local investments.
"MCI's view is that the merger is going forward as planned," company spokesman Jim Monroe said. "We are still hopeful that the we are going to close the merger by the fall," he said.
"(British Telecom) has been in alliance with us for four years, they hold board positions and they have a clear view of the announcements we made yesterday," Monroe said.
But a BT spokesman said earlier Friday MCI's earnings announcement had created a "complex situation" and did not rule out renegotiating terms for the more than $20 billion merger.
Late Thursday afternoon MCI announced that 1997 losses due to heavy investments in building U.S. local service networks could surpass $800 million, or double its previous estimates.

The U.S. long distance carrier said these losses would depress earnings for the rest of 1997 and 1998 but nonetheless it planned to push ahead with plans to position itself to compete in U.S. local markets.
The MCI spokesman said his company had held a board meeting on Wednesday at which plans to issue the comments about future earnings were discussed.
British Telecom Chief Executive Sir Peter Bonfield sits on MCI's board.
